name: Auris Adaptive Turtleneck
description:
A slim-profile turtleneck from Auris that regulates its own insulation based on ambient temperature — the smart-fiber weave reads external conditions and adjusts the loft of its internal structure passively, no app required, no battery. At room temperature it drapes like a fine-gauge merino knit. In cold, it thickens almost imperceptibly. The fabric has a very slight sheen — not flashy, but noticeable in good light. Available in black, deep green, graphite, and a warm rust that sold out immediately.

Auris markets this as 'quiet intelligence' and the branding is accurate: there's nothing visible about the tech, no logos beyond a small embossed tab at the back neck. It's the kind of shirt a Tier 4 professional wears under a jacket and nobody knows anything about it except that the person wearing it never seems to be too hot or cold. That's the point.
functionality: Passive thermal regulation — adjusts insulation loft in response to ambient temperature without external power source or app control.
what_it_says: Subtle, considered, someone who invests in things that work invisibly — comfort as a form of quiet status.
worn_by: consultants who travel between climate zones
story_hooks: A batch of Auris turtlenecks was recalled quietly — the adaptive fiber in that run responds to stress hormones, not just temperature, and several wearers noticed it getting tighter during arguments.
A Tier 4 executive was found dead, still perfectly comfortable-looking in an Auris turtleneck, in a room that had been at freezing temperatures for two days — the shirt had kept adjusting.
Someone is selling Auris seconds on a grey market platform; the adaptive function still works but the fiber degrades faster and starts to feel wrong against skin after six months.

physical_description.visual_profile: A refined, understated turtleneck with subtle luminescence in certain angles. The silhouette is sleek and body-conscious without being restrictive — it moves with the wearer rather than clinging. The high collar sits snugly at the throat with a refined finish. Overall impression is professional restraint with barely-perceptible technical sophistication.
physical_description.fit: Slim, contoured fit through the torso and shoulders. Not compression-tight, but form-following. Sleeves taper gently to the wrist. The turtleneck collar is firm but not choking — engineered for comfort across repeated wear cycles.
physical_description.primary_material: Smart-fiber synthetic blend — primarily phase-change microfiber composite mimicking high-grade merino wool. Internal loft structure is algorithmic at the fiber level; shifts density response passively based on thermal conditions.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, fine-gauge knit surface with minimal pilling potential. Subtle matte finish at rest; develops a faint sheen under direct light. Touch is soft and slightly cool to bare skin. At microscopic level, the weave shows deliberate irregularity — intentionally 'imperfect' to appear organic.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary options: pure black (most common, unremarkable), deep forest green (subtle luxury read), graphite gray (corporate neutral), warm rust-oxide (limited run, collector's item among Tier 3-4). Colors are flat and non-reflective unless caught in side-lighting.
physical_description.closures: None — pullover design. No visible seams on front or sides; construction suggests zero-waste manufacturing.
distinctive_features: Embossed Auris Textiles tab at back neck collar — small, tactile, no visible branding
Internal thermal-responsive fiber structure (invisible, passive, no electronics)
Seamless shoulder construction for unrestricted arm mobility
Slight horizontal micro-ribbing visible only under magnification
Collar edge finished with integrated binding that never rolls
Faint iridescence in certain angles — byproduct of smart-fiber weave, not intentional
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 boundary. Expensive enough to signal disposable income and access to corpo-subsidiary retail, but unmarked enough to avoid ostentatious display. Commonly seen in corpo office settings, transit terminals, medical facility staff.
physical_description.cultural_context: The wearer is someone who values invisible optimization over visible status. Worn by: mid-level corporate professionals, private sector technicians, independent consultants, medical practitioners, anyone who needs to maintain controlled body temperature across variable environments without drawing attention. Anti-hype positioning is itself aspirational among Tier 3 professionals.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to gently worn. The smart-fiber maintains its appearance across seasons — no pilling, no fading, no visible stress points. A year of daily wear looks like a month of regular use. Collars on vintage examples may show soft creasing from repeated wear, which paradoxically increases value among cognoscenti.

image_prompt: Neo-noir fashion photography: Auris Adaptive Turtleneck on a professional-appearing model, Tier 3 street casual, posed against rain-slicked industrial architecture. The turtleneck's fabric catches moody blue-and-amber neon from overhead, revealing its faint sheen. Shot in three-quarter profile, model's augmented wrist visible (discrete chrome accent). Lighting emphasizes the fabric's thermal-responsive micro-texture. Urban backdrop: wet concrete, geometric shadow, distant GLMZ skyline. Cool color grade, slight chromatic aberration. Emphasis on the garment's quiet confidence — no visible logos, no flashy elements, just understated technical elegance. --ar 2:3 --v 6
